record.paper_title: Some Properties of and Open Problems on Hessian Nilpotent Polynomials
record.original_question: Let C^n carry the standard C-bilinear form <., .>, and let X(C^n) be the set of isotropic vectors alpha with <alpha, alpha> = 0. Let P(z) be a homogeneous harmonic polynomial of degree d >= 2 over C written as P(z) = sum_{i=1}^k h_{alpha_i}(z)^d, where h_alpha(z) = <alpha, z> and each alpha_i lies in X(C^n). Define the graph G(P) to have vertex set {1, 2, ..., k}, with vertices i and j joined by an edge exactly when <alpha_i, alpha_j> is nonzero; regard G(P) as labeled when an edge i--j is assigned the value <alpha_i, alpha_j>, and in the even-degree variant when the edge label is h_{alpha_i}(z)^((d-2)/2) <alpha_i, alpha_j> h_{alpha_j}(z)^((d-2)/2). What necessary or sufficient conditions on this labeled graph G(P) ensure that P(z) is Hessian nilpotent?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Equip $\mathbb{C}^n$ with the standard symmetric $\mathbb{C}$-bilinear form $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ given by $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^n u_i v_i$, and let $X(\mathbb{C}^n)=\{\alpha\in\mathbb{C}^n:\langle\alpha,\alpha\rangle=0\}$ denote the set of isotropic vectors. For $\alpha\in\mathbb{C}^n$ set $h_\alpha(z)=\langle\alpha,z\rangle\in\mathbb{C}[z_1,\dots,z_n]$. A polynomial $P(z)\in\mathbb{C}[z_1,\dots,z_n]$ is called Hessian nilpotent if its Hessian matrix $\mathrm{Hess}(P)=\bigl(\partial^2 P/\partial z_i\partial z_j\bigr)$ is a nilpotent matrix over $\mathbb{C}[z_1,\dots,z_n]$.

Fix an integer $d\geq 2$ and let $P(z)$ be a homogeneous harmonic polynomial of degree $d$ (i.e., $\Delta P=0$ where $\Delta=\sum_i\partial^2/\partial z_i^2$) written in the form
$$P(z)=\sum_{i=1}^{k} h_{\alpha_i}(z)^{d}, \qquad \alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_k\in X(\mathbb{C}^n).$$

Associate to $P$ the labeled graph $G(P)$ with vertex set $[k]=\{1,2,\dots,k\}$ defined by: vertices $i\neq j$ are joined by an edge if and only if $\langle\alpha_i,\alpha_j\rangle\neq 0$. Consider two labelings of the edges of $G(P)$:

(i) the scalar labeling, where edge $i\text{--}j$ is labeled by $\langle\alpha_i,\alpha_j\rangle\in\mathbb{C}$;

(ii) for even $d$, the polynomial labeling, where edge $i\text{--}j$ is labeled by $h_{\alpha_i}(z)^{(d-2)/2}\,\langle\alpha_i,\alpha_j\rangle\,h_{\alpha_j}(z)^{(d-2)/2}\in\mathbb{C}[z_1,\dots,z_n]$.

Find necessary or sufficient conditions, formulated purely in terms of the combinatorics of the labeled graph $G(P)$ (under either labeling), which ensure that $P(z)$ is Hessian nilpotent.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is presented as an open problem in the study of Hessian nilpotent polynomials, motivated by the Jacobian conjecture. Partial results exist (e.g., complete descriptions of the graphs of HN polynomials when the span of the isotropic vectors has dimension at most 2 or at least s−2), but a full graph-theoretic characterization in general remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Two results on homogeneous Hessian nilpotent polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: For cases where the dimension of the span of isotropic vectors is at most 2 or at least s−2, complete descriptions of the graphs of polynomials with nilpotent Hessian exist.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial graph-theoretic characterizations of Hessian nilpotency are known.

status_evidence.title: Hessian Nilpotent Polynomials and the Jacobian Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Hessian nilpotent polynomials are linked to the Jacobian conjecture; structural questions remain open.
status_evidence.claim: General characterization questions about HN polynomials remain open.
